name: 360-degree squishy playground
purpose: Contact-driven three-dimensional sensory play with directional pokes, full-hand hold/squeeze, bounded two-contact pull and full azimuth orbit.
on_enter: Resolve draft, immutable saved record or explicit sample. Construct a closed 3D shape using the recipe and seed.
Restore only draft.playView yaw/pitch. Keep the separate photo camera unchanged.
Load hand-guide art and a cushion. Live body and hands are real procedural 3D geometry.
on_exit: Cancel contacts and pointer capture. Checkpoint recipe and draft camera only. Never persist live vertices, a contact or a half-complete hand pose.
persistence: Draft playView {yaw,pitch} is independent of photoOptions; saved records and thumbnails stay immutable. Gesture meshes and hands are transient. Existing idempotent material trials remain; no per-touch coins.
back_rule: Back goes 08 for draft, 11 for saved, 02 for sample. Finish goes 10 for draft; saved shows Photo/view option without new completion reward; sample offers Make to create a real draft.
acceptance: Six closed three-dimensional shapes; full 360-degree yaw and pitch from -89 to +89 with top and underside views.
Visible-surface perspective-correct picking on deformed triangles, including after the camera reaches the back.
Distinct fingertip poke, full five-digit mitten hold/squeeze and two-contact pull, with accessible single-pointer/button alternatives.
Stretch bounded to 0.67–1.50; documented active deformation volume ratio within 2%; exact recovery at material deadline.
No duplicate trial after two-contact release, cancellation, pause or repeated update. Third contact cannot steal either accepted contact.
Photo camera and immutable saved records are untouched by playground orbit. Backup/import validates playView.
WebGL smooth shading is primary; Canvas projection is a lower-fidelity fallback. Browser/device/GPU tests remain release gates.
implementation_notes: The v0.4 prototype uses analytic 3D deformation and enclosed-volume rescaling. It is not XPBD, measured material physics, photoreal skin or authored production topology.
ImageGen turntables are artist references, not calibrated angle samples or runtime geometry. The runtime orbit is continuous.
Procedural hand geometry renders in the same depth-tested scene; optional sprite sheets are guides and rig references.
Production targets include tetrahedral XPBD/contact constraints, retopology/UVs, skinned hand IK/collision, refined transmission and target-device profiling.
See scene09-3d-spec.md and scene09-3d-validation.json for delivered scope and open verification.

actions.trigger: Pointerdown/move/up on visible hero; max two active contacts
actions.guard: Play mode; raycast hits live proxy; pointer ID not already captured
actions.command: Perspective-correct surface pick, then contact-driven 3D poke/hold/pull
actions.state_write: Transient vertices and hands only; existing material-trial qualification on complete recovery
actions.feedback: Local inward dent or volume-corrected squeeze/stretch; procedural hand follows anchor
actions.interrupt: pointercancel/lostcapture/orientation=release; one contact ending from stretch blends into single contact. Ignore third contact for the entire gesture.
